Module Seven Activity¶

For the module seven activity, you will identify relevant data and write Python code to generate visualizations and interpret insights from the provided data set. Professionals in data-driven fields must not only interpret data but also gather, analyze, and present it in meaningful and actionable ways. This activity allows you to practice these essential skills by working through the complete exploratory data analysis (EDA) process.

Note: there are two parts to this assignment. Part One is the coding activity. Part Two is the written report.

Once your code is complete, you will download this notebook as an HTML file by clicking File, then Download As, then HTML (.html) from the Jupyter menu bar. Validate that your code, output, and all visualizations (rendered as images using the display() function) are visible in the html file before submission.

Missing Blocks: Ensure that you have clicked Run for all blocks before downloading as an HTML file or the block may be missing from your submission. Images must be called using the display() function, for example: display(Image(filename="output/{image_name}.png"))

Specifically, you must address the items from the rubric criteria.

Part One: Python Code¶

In this part, you will write Python code to analyze the data and generate visualizations that explore trends.

Create multiple, distinct visualizations that explore different aspects of the data using Python Libraries.¶

Include the following:

  • Code comments explaining each step of your analysis

Part Two: Report¶

In this part, you will write a reflection to explain the insights gained from your analysis and visualizations. This part is to be completed in a word document, using the output here to answer the topics.

  • Explain the trends, differences, or outliers you observed in the data.
  • Describe any disparities or patterns that may be relevant to the nonprofit’s goals.
  • Write a summary of what the data suggests about transit usage across neighborhoods.
  • Explain how the visualizations support your conclusions.
  • Discuss how your findings could inform the nonprofit’s decision-making or strategy.
  • Describe the importance of data-driven insights in addressing real-world challenges.

# To Do: Convert numeric columns to proper formats (removing commas and extra spaces)

# Numeric columns: 'NTD ID', 'Legacy NTD ID', 'UACE CD', 'UZA SQ Miles', 'UZA Population',
# 'Service Area Population', 'Service Area SQ Miles', 'Passenger Miles FY', 'Unlinked 
# Passenger Trips FY', 'Avg Trip Length FY', 'Fares FY', 'Operating Expenses FY',
# 'Avg Cost Per Trip FY', 'Avg Fares Per Trip FY'

# Date columns: 'Last Closed Report Year', 'Last Closed FY End Month', 'Last Closed FY End Year'

# Non-numeric columns: 'Agency', 'Mode', 'TOS', '3 Mode', 'Mode/Type of Service Status',
# 'Reporter Type', 'Organization Type', 'HQ City, 'HQ State', 'UZA Name'

numeric_columns = ['NTD ID', 'Legacy NTD ID', 'UACE CD', 'UZA SQ Miles', 'UZA Population',
'Service Area Population', 'Service Area SQ Miles', 'Passenger Miles FY', 'Unlinked Passenger Trips FY', 
'Avg Trip Length FY', 'Fares FY', 'Operating Expenses FY','Avg Cost Per Trip FY', 'Avg Fares Per Trip FY']

# To remove commas
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Passenger Miles FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Passenger Miles FY'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Unlinked Passenger Trips FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Unlinked Passenger Trips FY'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)

# To remove dollar signs
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Avg Cost Per Trip FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Avg Cost Per Trip FY'].astype(str).str.replace('[$]', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Avg Fares Per Trip FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Avg Fares Per Trip FY'].astype(str).str.replace('[$]', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)

# To remove dollar signs and commas
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Fares FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Fares FY'].astype(str).str.replace('[$|,]', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Operating Expenses FY'] = pd.to_numeric(data_file_cleaned['Operating Expenses FY'].astype(str).str.replace('[$|,]', '', regex=True),errors='coerce',)

# To convert date information to the proper format
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Last Closed Report Year'] = pd.to_datetime(data_file_cleaned['Last Closed Report Year'].astype(int).astype(str), format='%Y')
data_file_cleaned.loc[:,'Last Closed FY End Year'] = pd.to_datetime(data_file_cleaned['Last Closed FY End Year'].astype(int).astype(str), format='%Y')

# To add a column to the dataset to classify the information based on the size of the 
# population into city classification groups

conditions = [cleaned_data['City Population'] <= 200000,
    (cleaned_data['City Population'] > 200000) & (cleaned_data['City Population'] <= 500000),
    (cleaned_data['City Population'] > 500000) & (cleaned_data['City Population'] <= 1500000),
    cleaned_data['City Population'] > 1500000,]

choices = ['Small Urban Area','Medium-Size Urban Area',
    'Metropolitan Area','Large Metropolitan Area',]

cleaned_data['Location Type'] = np.select(conditions, choices, default='Other')

# To create National figure showing the breakdown of Total Public Transport Trips
# per Location Type (Small Urban Area, Medium-Size Urban Area, Metropolitan Area,
# and Large Metropolitan Area)

visual_1df = cleaned_data.copy()

# To filter the data for 2023 

visual_1df['Year'] = pd.to_datetime(visual_1df['Year'], format='%Y')
visual_1df_2023 = visual_1df[visual_1df['Year'].dt.year == 2023]

# Color-blind friendly colors

colors= ["#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7"]

# Location for file output

output_dir = "output"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "pie_chart_national.png")

# Create the pie chart

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 8))

location_type =visual_1df_2023.groupby('Location Type')['Total Public Transport Trips'].sum()
location_type.plot(kind='pie', autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=colors,pctdistance=1.10,labeldistance=1.25)

# Add labels and title

plt.title('Total Public Transport Trips by City Type in 2023', pad=35)
plt.ylabel('') 

plt.pie(location_type, labels=None, autopct=None, startangle=90)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(output_path, bbox_inches="tight", dpi=100)
plt.close()

# Use the display() function to render the generated png image in the html output
display(Image(filename="output/pie_chart_national.png"))

# Note: the purpose of this figure is to provide comparison information 
# regarding each of the three neighborhoods and the relevant comparison
# neighborhoods. The comparison neighborhoods were chosen based on being
# located in WA or OR and having a population size similar that of one of 
# three neighbhorhoods being analyszed

# Below is the neighhorhood along with the comparison neighorhood:
# 1) King County -> Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon
# 2) Spokane Transit Authority -> Lane Transit District
# 3) City of Longview -> Skagit Transit
In [27]:
# To create a grouped bar chart comparing the service area population to the 
# total city/neighbhorhood population. This will allow a comparison to be made
# between each neighborhood as well as between each individul neighbhorhood
# and it's comparison neighbhorhood

visual_7df = cleaned_data.copy()

# To filter the data to include the relevant neighbhorhoods

visual_7df = visual_7df[visual_7df['Location'].isin(["King County", "City of Longview",
"Spokane Transit Authority","Skagit Transit", "Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon",
"Lane Transit District"])]

# To filter the data for 2023

visual_7df['Year'] = pd.to_datetime(visual_7df['Year'], format='%Y')
visual_7df_2023 = visual_7df[visual_7df['Year'].dt.year == 2023]

# To calculate the Service Area Population as a Percentage of the City Population
# for the relevant neighbhorhoods and their comparison neighbhorhoods

visual_7df['Service Area %'] = visual_7df['Service Area Population'] / visual_7df['City Population']

visual_7df = visual_7df.sort_values(by='Location Type')

# Color-blind friendly colors

colors= ["#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73"]

# Location for file output

output_dir = "output"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "comparison_bar_chart.png")

# Creating order of bar chart columns

bar_chart_order = ['City of Longview', 'Skagit Transit', 'Spokane Transit Authority', 'Lane Transit District',
                  'King County', 'Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon']

# Create the bar chart

sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 18))
ax = sns.barplot(
    data=visual_7df,
    x='Location',
    y='Service Area %',
    hue='Location Type',
    palette=colors,
    dodge=True,
    order=bar_chart_order,
)

# Add labels and title

plt.title('Service Area as a Percentage of Neighborhood Population',fontweight='bold', pad=20, fontsize=20)
plt.xlabel('Neighborhood')
plt.ylabel('Service Area as a % of City Population', labelpad=60)
plt.legend(title='Population Type')

for container in ax.containers:
  ax.bar_label(container, padding=3, fmt='{:.1%}')
    
ax.axhline(y=1.00, color='red')

ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))

ax.set_ylabel("Service Area\n as a Percentage\n of City Population\n (in %)", rotation=0, fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel("Neighborhood", rotation=0, fontweight='bold')

plt.xticks(ticks=[0.27, 1.25, 2, 3, 3.75, 4.75], labels=["City of\nLongview", "Comp:\n Skagit Transit", "Spokane Transit\n Authority", 
"Comp:\nLane Transit\n District", "King\nCounty", "Comp:\n Tri-County"], rotation=0, ha ='center')

# Save the plot to a png file in the 'output'folder

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(output_path, bbox_inches="tight", dpi=100)

# Note: the purpose of this figure is to examine the operating expenses of the 
# three neighbhorhoods part of this analysis. The analysis should account for
# longer trips,in terms of miles, having higher operating expenses. Therefore the 
# Average Trip Length column will be used to calculate the average cost per mile 
# on the given public transportation. This figure will compare the regional average
# with the local, or neighbhorhood, average cost per mile 

visual_8df = cleaned_data.copy()

# To filter the data for WA and OR

visual_8df = visual_8df[visual_8df['HQ State'].isin(['WA', 'OR'])]

# To filter the data for 2023

visual_8df['Year'] = pd.to_datetime(visual_8df['Year'], format='%Y')
visual_8df_2023 = visual_8df[visual_8df['Year'].dt.year == 2023]

# To calculate the average cost per mile on each type of public transportation

visual_8df['Cost per Mile'] = visual_8df['Average Cost per Trip'].values / visual_8df['Average Trip Length'].values

# To find the average Cost per Mile for each Mode Type in WA and OR

visual_8df_pivoted_regional = visual_8df.groupby(['Mode Type'])['Cost per Mile'].mean().reset_index() 

visual_8df_pivoted_regional['Location'] = 'Regional'

# To find the average Cost per Mile for each of the three neighborhoods

visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood = visual_8df.groupby(['Mode Type', 'Location'])['Cost per Mile'].mean().reset_index()

visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood = visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood[visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood['Location'].isin(["King County", 
"City of Longview","Spokane Transit Authority"])]

visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood_average = (visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood.groupby("Mode Type")["Cost per Mile"].mean().reset_index())
                                                                           
visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood_average ['Location'] = 'Neighborhood'

# Combining regional and neighborhood averages into one dataset

combined_df = pd.concat([visual_8df_pivoted_regional, visual_8df_pivoted_neighborhood_average], ignore_index=True)

# Color-blind friendly colors

colors= ["#0072B2", "#D55E00"]

# Location for file output

output_dir = "output"
os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "regional_cost_per_mile_bar_chart.png")

# Create the bar chart

sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid')
plt.figure(figsize=(20, 15))
ax = sns.barplot(data=combined_df, x='Mode Type', y='Cost per Mile', hue='Location', palette=colors, dodge=True)

for container in ax.containers:
  ax.bar_label(container, padding=3, fmt='${:,.2f}')

# Add labels and title

plt.title('Comparison of Average Cost per Mile per Mode Type (Regional vs. Neighhorhood)', fontweight='bold', pad=20, fontsize=20)
plt.xlabel("Mode Type", fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel("Average Cost\n per Mile\n (in dollars ($))", fontweight="bold", rotation=0)

plt.gca().yaxis.set_major_formatter(ticker.StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.2f}'))

# Save the plot to a png file in the 'output'folder

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig(output_path, bbox_inches="tight", dpi=100)
plt.close()

# Use the display() function to render the generated png image in the html output

display(Image(filename="output/regional_cost_per_mile_bar_chart.png"))
